## Purpose

Assess whether the current evidence shows that the Lead Lab Option B deliverable meets the approved acceptance boundary. This run prepares an objective acceptance matrix and exceptions record. It does not accept the deliverable, close gaps, change scope, assign owners, approve production readiness, or start CHG-02 implementation.

## Acceptance Boundary

The assessment covers every approved in-scope requirement named in the acceptance matrix. It also records the unresolved outcome for `RQ-17` (embedded-video URL protection) and the decision status for `RQ-18` (Microsoft 365 SSO should be used for the new application), as required by the scope baseline's acceptance boundary.

## Tailoring Decision

| Factor | Project evidence | Effect on rigor |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | The application must protect participant content and be available before 2026-09-11. | Acceptance evidence is required. |
| Scale | The delivery team and product are small, but the approved MVP spans access, community, classroom, calendar, administration, security, and operations. | Standard traceability is sufficient for this review; full formal launch acceptance remains later. |
| Duration | The schedule is short and the Gate 1 control trigger has moved to next week. | Use a compact matrix with clear evidence gaps and retest triggers. |
| Complexity | Authentication, participant data, staging, operations, video behavior, and CHG-02 affect acceptance. | Record dependencies and exceptions instead of treating missing evidence as a pass. |
| Approach | The application is being built iteratively from a local vertical slice toward staging. | Validate the current increment without treating it as the complete MVP. |
| Authority | The requester and IT team prepare and test; the LeadLab Director gives final launch acceptance. | Keep acceptance, closure, ownership, and baseline decisions outside this draft. |

## Minimum Output

1. Acceptance matrix for the approved Option B requirements.
2. Evidence status for the local vertical slice, staging, browser, responsive, participant, and operational checks.
3. Explicit exceptions for `RQ-17` (embedded-video URL protection), `RQ-18` (Microsoft 365 SSO should be used for the new application), and CHG-02 (Add an administrator Classroom link and session recordings page).
4. Acceptance authority, proposed process metadata changes, and next trigger.

## Authority Boundary

The IT team prepares and records test evidence. The requester and IT team provide scope direction. The LeadLab Director gives final launch acceptance. Alson may assess evidence and prepare proposed records, but may not accept the deliverable, close related items, change the agreed scope, assign owners, revise a baseline, or approve production readiness.
